To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single intraamniotic injection of Et-DHA during the late gestational period in the rat reduces the ability of fetal brains to form Fe 3+mediated LPO, and enhances PGE 2 and TxB 3 production, while reducing the formation of free radicals.
a single intra-amiotic injection of Et-DHA to pregnant rats enhances the production of PGE 2 and TxB2 and reduces LPO in fetal brain.
a single intrauterine injection of DHA reduces the ability of fetal rat brain slices to generate Fe 2+ -mediated LPO and increases the production of TxB  and PGE .
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of DHA in the regulation of lipid peroxidation during development.
the study of the mechanisms by which DHA administration to fetuses during the late stage of gestation enhances the antioxidant capability of the developing brain.
the role of polyunsaturated fatty acids in the modulation of the oxidative stress in the fetal rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antioxidant activity of DHA may be related to the ability to divert damaging radicals to a less harmful metabolic route.
the beneficial effect of DHA on the fetal rat brain may be due to a combination of its antioxidant and prostanoid production enhancing properties.
DHA is a very effective antioxidant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DHA is not a pro-oxidant but a potent anti-oxidant in vivo, and that the anti-oxidant activity is due to a combination of factors.
DHA administration during intrauterin life enhances the production of prostanoid and reduces the generation of free radicals in the fetal brain.

DHA administration in vivo during the last third of gestation enhances the prostanoid formation in fetal brain, and this effect is associated with a reduction in the formation of Fe 2+ -induced lipid peroxides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DHA may be able to prevent the development of neurological diseases in which free radicals are implicated.
DHA administration to the fetus may be a useful tool to reduce the oxidative stress and to enhance the prostanoid production in the fetal brain.
DHA is an important antioxidant in the developing brain.
